scientific_question: Does bidirectional cardinality actuation replicate across the historically selected candidate-head pool, rather than being unique to L18H13?
candidate_pool_origin: historical fixed seven-head candidate pool; not selected using Experiment D outcomes

dataset.name: proc_count_multi_actuator_d1_v1
dataset.freshness_requirement: zero seed overlap and zero exact image-hash overlap with proc_count_causal_v1/v2/v3/v4

primary_reporting.formal_directional_tests: one-sided exact binomial tests versus 0.5 for downward and upward consistency
primary_reporting.multiplicity: Holm correction across the 14 directional tests (7 heads x 2 directions)
primary_reporting.bidirectional_replication_definition: both downward and upward directional tests remain significant after Holm correction

interpretation.primary: report the number and identity of historical candidate heads showing fresh bidirectional replication
not_claimed: that L18H13 is not stronger than alternatives
that any alternative head is universally superior
that candidate prevalence estimates head prevalence

pre_inference_implementation_correction.reason: The D1 generator was mechanically derived from the v4 N=2000 generator. D1 intentionally uses 10 counts x 5 conditions x 6 replicates = N=300, but inherited terminal validation still required N=2000.
pre_inference_implementation_correction.correction: Replace inherited fixed N=2000 validation with EXPECTED_N = 10 * len(CONDITIONS) * REPLICATES.

pre_inference_implementation_correction_.reason: Remaining validation constants 400, 200, and 40 were inherited from the v4 40-replicate design.
